'''Noh Tae-won''' ({{Korean|hangul=노태원}}; born August 4, 1957) is a South Korean physicist and director of the Center for Correlated Electron Systems (CCES) in the [[Institute for Basic Science]] (IBS) at [[Seoul National University]] (SNU). He has published more than 400 papers and been cited 15,000 times. He is a member of the [[Materials Research Society]], Korean Optical Society, Korean Crystallographic Society, and Association of Asia Pacific Physical Societies and has been on several editorial boards for journals. In 2017, he became president of the Korean Dielectrics Society.<ref name=":recfi-snu">{{cite web |url= http://recfi.snu.ac.kr/pagegenerater.asp?catalogid=rcfi&language=en&pagecode=sub02_01 |title= Professor |author=<!--Not stated--> |access-date= 15 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://kdsnet.or.kr/skin/page/about01.html |script-title=ko:인사말 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 1 June 2018 |website= Korean Dielectrics Society (한국유전체연구회) |access-date= 1 July 2019 |language= ko}}</ref> In 2024, he became the 9th president of the [[Korea Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://physics.snu.ac.kr/boards/news?md=v&bbsidx=12219 |script-title=ko:[노태원 명예교수] 고등과학원장으로 임명 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Physics Department |publisher= [[Seoul National University]] |access-date= 10 June 2024 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref>

==Education==
Noh graduated from [[Kyunggi High School]] in [[Seoul]], South Korea, in 1976 and received his B.Sc. (1982) in [[Physics]] from Seoul National University. Supervised by Dr. James R. Gaine, he obtained his M.S. and Ph.D. in physics from [[Ohio State University]] in 1984 and 1986, respectively.

==Career==
Noh conducted postdoctoral research in Dr. Albert John Sievers' group at [[Cornell University]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Noh |first1= T. W. |last2= Sulewski |first2= P. E. |last3= Kaplan |first3= S. G. |last4= Sievers |first4= A. J. |last5= Lathrop |first5= D. K. |last6= Buhrman |first6= R. A. |title= Far infrared measurements on single crystals, films and bulk sintered high temperature superconductors |url= https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mrs-online-proceedings-library-archive/article/far-infrared-measurements-on-single-crystals-films-and-bulk-sintered-high-temperature-superconductors/352F5CC689CE8CC210240EE483854D98 |journal= MRS Online Proceedings Library Archive |year= 1987 |volume= 99 |issue= 435 |article-number= 435 |doi= 10.1557/PROC-99-435 |access-date= 1 July 2019 |url-access= subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= Sulewski |first1= P. E. |last2= Noh |first2= T. W. |last3= McWhirter |first3= J. T. |last4= Sievers |first4= A. J. |title= Far-infrared composite-medium study of sintered La2NiO4 and La1.85Sr0.15CuO4−y |url= https://journals.aps.org/prb/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevB.36.5735 |journal= Physical Review B |year= 1987 |volume= 36 |issue= 10 |pages= 5735–5738 |doi= 10.1103/PhysRevB.36.5735 |pmid= 9942247 |access-date= 1 July 2019 |url-access= subscription }}</ref> until 1989.<ref name=":pdsnu"/> During that period, he studied the optical properties of [[High-temperature superconductivity|high-Tc superconductors]], especially [[copper oxide]]. In August 1989, he joined the faculty of the Department of Physics at Seoul National University starting as an assistant professor before becoming an associate and later full professor.

He was the director of the Research Center for Oxide Electronics at SNU from 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/eng/sub02_03_01.do |title= Center for Correlated Electron Systems |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= Institute for Basic Science |access-date= 1 July 2019 }}</ref>

With funding from the Institute for Basic Science, he established the Center for Correlated Electron Systems at Seoul National University in 2012. The research center searches for new emerging phenomena at the interfaces of strongly correlated electron systems, such as oxides.

He became an Endowed-Chair Professor at SNU in 2017.<ref name=":pdsnu">{{cite web |url= http://physics.snu.ac.kr/research-faculty/faculty/fulltime?mode=view&profidx=24 |script-title=ko:노태원 교수 |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= Department of Physics |publisher=[[Seoul National University]] |access-date= 1 July 2019 }}</ref>

In 2019, the Center for Correlated Electron Systems and the Institute for Solid State Physics (ISSP) of the [[University of Tokyo]] opened a joint research laboratory at Seoul National University.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://ibs.re.kr/cop/bbs/BBSMSTR_000000000739/selectBoardArticle.do?nttId=17237 |title= South Korea-Japan partner on developing advanced laser photoelectron spectrometers |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 24 April 2019 |website= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 20 June 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.dt.co.kr/contents.html?article_no=2019041902109931731003 |title= IBS-日 고체물리연, 물성 연구 위한 '공동연구실' 개소 |last= 이 |first= 준기 |date= 19 April 2019 |website= 디지털타임스 |access-date= 20 June 2019 }}</ref>

Noh performs research in [[condensed matter physics]]. His research has focused on [[transition metal oxides]] but has extended to other strongly correlated electron systems. His research interests include the growth of oxide thin films and artificial [[heterostructure]]s, emerging phenomena in oxide surfaces and interfaces, the [[metal-insulator transition]] and orbital physics in transition metal oxides, the optical properties of numerous solids, and the physics of oxide devices such as ferroelectric random-access memory ([[ferroelectric RAM|FeRAM]]), resistance RAM ([[resistive random-access memory|RRAM]]), and spintronic devices.

He has worked on novel nanoscale physical phenomena, especially in informational devices such as [[ferroelectric RAM|FeRAM]]s and [[resistive random-access memory|RRAM]]s. He elucidated the physical mechanism of the fatigue problem in FeRAMs. He also addressed the critical thickness of ultrathin films where they lose [[ferroelectricity]]. Additionally, he sought to explain resistance-switching phenomena, which are the basis of RRAM. Recently, he developed a new percolation model, called the "random circuit-breaker network model", which can explain reversible switching phenomena. He also discovered a novel quantum state of the correlated electron system in iridates that has attracted the interest of many researchers. He investigated the Mott physics of Sr2IrO4, which has a Mott insulator phase in the Jeff = 1/2 state.

In the [[Korean Physical Society]] (KPS), he has served as treasurer (FY 1999–2000), executive officer (FY 2003–04), and vice president (FY 2009–12). He served as a council member trustee of the Association of Asia and Pacific Physical Societies from 2011 – 2013,<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.aapps.org/myboard/read.php?id=7&Page=1&Board=about_aapps |title= Council |author=<!--Not stated--> |publisher= Association of Asia and Pacific Physical Societies |access-date= 1 July 2019 }}</ref> is on the board of trustees at the Asia Pacific Center for Theoretical Physics,<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.apctp.org/sub4/index1_4.php |title= Organization Chart |author=<!--Not stated--> |publisher= Asia Pacific Center for Theoretical Physics |access-date= 1 July 2019 }}</ref> and the International Advisory Board of the Asian Meeting on Ferroelectricity.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://hiroshima2018.com/meeting-web/amf.html |title= International Advisory Board of AMF |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= 2018 ISAF-FMA-AMF-AMEC-PFM Joint Conference (IFAAP 2018) |access-date= 1 July 2019 }}</ref> In 2014, he became a member of the International Union of Physics and Applied Physics.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://iupap.org/c10-members-2014-2017/ |title= C10: MEMBERS (2014-2017) |author=<!--Not stated--> |publisher= International Union of Physics and Applied Physics |access-date= 1 July 2019 }}</ref> He has served on the editorial boards of several international journals, including ''[[Applied Physics Letters]]'', and as editor-in-chief of ''[[Current Applied Physics]]''.

==Conferences==
He has also helped to organize numerous international conferences as a member of international advisory or program committees. Noh was Chair of the 5th Korea–Japan Conference on Ferroelectricity (KJC-FE5, 2004), the International Workshop on Oxide Electronics (WOE-2007), and the Joint Conference of the Asian Meeting on Ferroelectricity and the Asian Meeting on Electroceramics (AMF-AMEC-2010). He has also served on the International Advisory or Program Committees of over 40 other international conferences. He has given over 100 invited talks at international conferences. He has also delivered plenary talks at international conferences, including IMF-11 (2005, Brazil), JKC-FE6 (2006, Japan), AAPC-11 (2010, China), KPS (2011, Busan), and AMEC (2012, Malaysia).
